children: Shares of Wipro Ltd. will be in focus on Thursday, November 26, after the IT services company announced a strategic supplier partnership with British energy major BP to transform the latter's core finance operations using artificial intelligence (AI) and automation.

As part of the agreement, around 3,000 BP employees supporting finance operations across India, Hungary and Malaysia will transition to Wipro. The new operating model is expected to become effective in 2027.

While the companies have not disclosed the financial details or tenure of the agreement, a report by Mint, citing sources, pegged the deal value at more than $500 million. The contract is expected to generate approximately $75 million in annual revenue for Wipro over the next six to seven years, according to the report.
CNBC-TV18 has not independently verified these details.
The agreement is a new contract and not an extension of an existing engagement, the report said. However, its meaningful revenue contribution is likely to begin only from FY28.
Brokerage firm Kotak Institutional Equities has maintained its 'Sell' rating on Wipro, with a price target of ₹155 per share, following the announcement.
The brokerage described the BP agreement as a new mega deal and said that Wipro would onboard around 3,000 employees supporting the energy major's finance operations across the three countries.

Kotak said the contract was one of two large deals that had been delayed from the previous quarter. It believes the agreement could help drive a recovery in Wipro's revenue, particularly as the company's Europe and Middle East (EMR) segment has seen revenues decline 36% since the first quarter of FY24.
However, the brokerage cautioned that competitive intensity remains elevated in the IT services industry, particularly for larger contracts. This could weigh on the initial phase of the engagement.

Kotak estimates that the BP deal could contribute less than 70-80 basis points to Wipro's annualised revenue. It added that the company would need to demonstrate sustained deal wins to provide greater visibility on its growth trajectory.
The brokerage also believes that Wipro's stock is trading at full valuations, limiting the scope for a more favourable view despite the new contract win.
Wipro shares settled 0.94% higher at ₹189.05 on Wednesday, November 25. However, the stock has declined around 30% so far in 2026.

title: Wipro shares gain 3% after over $500 million BP deal, but Kotak says 'sell'
